Q1: S-Ethyl dipropylthiocarbamate is classified with known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive toxicity (CMR), environmental concerns (ENV), and oral toxicity (ORL). It also shows evidence of endocrine disruption (Tier 2) and has demonstrated low to moderate inhalation hazards (Tier 3), though data is currently deficient for dermal/eye (SKN) and organ/systemic (OGN) hazards.
Q2: S-Ethyl dipropylthiocarbamate is identified on several "Lists of Concern," including California's Proposition 65 due to its potential to cause cancer or reproductive harm. It is also listed by the Endocrine Disruption Exchange as a potential endocrine disruptor and is recognized by the EPA as an active pesticide ingredient.
Q3: This chemical appears relatively well-characterized, with 2,769 literature references, significantly above the median for chemicals in our database, and a well-defined molecular formula (C9H19NOS) and substance class. However, its hazard profile is not entirely complete, as indicated by data deficiencies (Tier 4) for dermal/eye and organ/systemic hazards.
